content.title: Switch alert expansion and keep only one alert open
content.intent: Prove that when the user opens a second alert, the previously expanded alert collapses so no more than one alert is expanded at any time.
content.technique_notes: Applied state / flow because the source defines a before-and-after interaction across sequential alert openings. Applied boundary value analysis to the explicit expansion-count limit of at most one alert at a time; the relevant observable boundary states are 1 expanded alert and the attempted transition to 2, which must resolve back to 1 by collapsing the previous alert. No combinatorial covering array was needed because this path varies one interaction dimension rather than multiple independent inputs.

content.title: Expand one alert inline without turning the panel into a modal
content.intent: Prove that selecting an alert reveals its detail inline within the alerts list and preserves the list as a non-modal surface.
content.technique_notes: Applied state / flow because the source promises a collapsed-to-expanded state change on click. Kept this as a separate happy path from the single-expansion boundary case because expanding one alert proves inline expansion and non-modal behavior without involving the second-alert transition. No combinatorial covering array was needed because the path has no independent variable set to combine.

content.title: Review the default portfolio alerts feed
content.intent: Prove that the alerts panel presents the expected alert titles and the required per-alert fields with allowed severity labels.
content.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning to the displayed alert set and allowed severity vocabulary, using one review path to cover the required alert-title members and the required per-alert field classes. Kept the content review separate from interaction paths so the static feed-content promises can be proven without conflating them with expansion behavior. No combinatorial covering array was needed because the source defines a fixed alert list rather than independent input combinations.

judgements.rationale: [applicability] State / flow applied because the source explicitly defines click-driven state changes: inline expansion, a one-expanded-alert limit, and automatic collapse of the previously opened alert when another opens.

[applicability] Boundary value analysis applied to the explicit maximum of one expanded alert at once; the meaningful UI boundary is the attempt to exceed 1 by opening another alert while one is already expanded.

[applicability] Negative, auth, api-contract, concurrency, idempotency, persistence, perf, a11y, i18n, and notification techniques were not scenario-generating here because the cited source text states no invalid-input handling, gated access, backend contract, concurrent-write, retry, durability, timing, accessibility, localization, or out-of-band effect promises for this panel.
